name: boundary-rebalance-no-trade-band
rationale: shirube currently treats allocation_threshold as a trigger only: once |target - current| clears it, the position is rebalanced all the way back to target. Classical no-trade-region results under proportional transaction costs say the opposite is optimal — trade only far enough to reach the boundary of the no-trade band, never to its centre — and the 2026-09-12 baseline is exactly the regime where that distinction should bite. At 500,000 JPY the baseline made 754 trades in 14 days (53.9/day) with an 11.7% win rate, moved 42.9M JPY of notional on 500k of equity (86x turnover), paid fee_drag_pct 5.68% against a total return of -16.09%, and lost 13.25pp of return and 24.75 of Sharpe to its own exposure-matched static mix. Full-distance rebalancing is what makes each of those 754 trades as large as it can be, and because the target oscillates around the current allocation, an over-correction in one direction immediately manufactures the opposite delta — the same overshoot-into-reversal mechanism the 2026-09-11 report measured in min-notional-aware-rebalance (3,744 buys vs 4,751 sells). Rebalancing to the near edge instead leaves the position inside the band, so a small reversal of the signal no longer clears the threshold at all. This keeps the entry condition, the signal, and the zone mapping byte-for-byte identical and changes only how far each triggered rebalance travels, so the result is attributable to that one mechanism.
code_change_summary: Change how far a triggered rebalance travels, without changing when one triggers. Today both the live path (TradingEngine::handle_indicator and the periodic-rebalance path in src/trading/engine.rs, the two sites around lines 485 and 562 that test `delta.abs() < allocation_threshold`) and the backtest path (Simulator::run in src/backtest/simulator.rs, the `delta.abs() >= trading_config.allocation_threshold` test) pass the FULL `delta` to TradingEngine::allocation_delta_to_order, which rebalances all the way to target. Add one new pub(crate) associated function on TradingEngine, e.g. `fn band_edge_delta(delta: f64, allocation_threshold: f64) -> f64`, that returns the distance to the near edge of the no-trade band rather than to its centre: if `delta.abs() < allocation_threshold` return 0.0 (caller must not trade), otherwise return `delta - delta.signum() * allocation_threshold`. Document it with the formula, the [0, |delta|] range of the magnitude it returns, and a NOTE citing this hypothesis and the classical proportional-cost no-trade-region result. Then, at ALL THREE call sites above, keep the existing threshold test exactly as it is and pass `Self::band_edge_delta(delta, allocation_threshold)` (or `TradingEngine::band_edge_delta(...)` in the simulator) to allocation_delta_to_order in place of the raw `delta`. Do not change allocation_delta_to_order itself, the threshold comparison, the sign/side derivation (band_edge_delta preserves delta's sign whenever it is non-zero), compute_btc_target, apply_zone, the sticky_target logic, the RiskManager call sequence, or the orders_below_min counting arm. Note in your report that this change necessarily shrinks every order by allocation_threshold of equity, which at the 50,000 JPY primary capital pushes more orders under the 0.001 BTC lot floor (the baseline already suppressed 5,960 there) — that is a real effect of the mechanism, not a bug, but it must be quantified via orders_below_min rather than left implicit. Add unit tests in src/trading/engine.rs's test module covering: a positive delta above threshold (returns delta - threshold, strictly less than delta, same sign), a negative delta below -threshold (returns delta + threshold, same sign), a delta exactly at +threshold (returns 0.0), a sub-threshold delta (returns 0.0), and an end-to-end assertion that an order built from band_edge_delta is strictly smaller than one built from the raw delta for the same equity and price.
constraints: This hypothesis does NOT need to modify the body of TradingEngine::compute_btc_target, and MUST NOT do so — the signal is held fixed so the measured effect is attributable to the sizing change alone.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) or its body.

MUST NOT change the threshold entry condition itself — `delta.abs() >= allocation_threshold` stays exactly as it is at every call site, so this variant triggers on precisely the same candles as the baseline.

MUST apply the change at ALL THREE call sites (both live sites in src/trading/engine.rs and the one in src/backtest/simulator.rs), so the backtest cannot measure a strategy the live engine would not run. Leaving the live path unchanged would make the backtest result meaningless.
MUST NOT change TradingEngine::allocation_delta_to_order, the exchange lot-size check, or the fee logic.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the existing compute_btc_target_* and simulator tests in src/trading/engine.rs and src/backtest/simulator.rs — update an expected value only where the new sizing legitimately changes it (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically — a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff changes order sizing on the LIVE order-submission path, per the 'anything touching live trading behavior gets flagged explicitly' rule in docs/self-improvement-loop.md.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the bitFlyer REST/WS client.

paper_reference.title: Optimal two-parameter portfolio management strategy with transaction costs
paper_reference.key_claim: Under a trading-frequency cost proxy, a no-trade band applied directly to an unsmoothed signal — holding the position unchanged inside the band, so the policy has hysteresis — is locally optimal, and dominates smoothing the signal and then thresholding it: the band alone minimises trading frequency subject to a fixed return constraint.
paper_reference.pros: It isolates the exact lever shirube leaves on the table. shirube already has the band's entry half (allocation_threshold) but none of its hysteresis: it snaps back to the centre on every trigger, so the position is never left resting inside the band and a small signal reversal immediately re-triggers. The paper's mechanism is the cheapest possible remedy — no new signal, no new indicator, no new config field — and it targets the deficit the 2026-09-12 baseline actually shows (754 trades, 86x turnover, 11.7% win rate, -24.75 Sharpe against a one-trade static mix at 500,000 JPY), which is a turnover problem rather than a signal problem.
paper_reference.cons: Do not trust the result at face value here. The paper's portfolio is binary long/short (+1/-1) whereas shirube holds a continuous [0,1] BTC allocation, so 'rebalance to the boundary' is a construction the paper never analyses. Its signals are synthetic Gaussian AR(1) processes with no empirical validation on any market, let alone BTC/JPY at 1-minute resolution. It deliberately declines to model transaction costs at all, using trading frequency as a proxy — which is precisely the approximation that made shirube's own pre-#14 numbers wrong by ~19.5pp, since cost depends on notional traded and not only on trade count. Its price model is a standard rather than geometric random walk. And critically, the doc's own 'Benchmarks' section establishes that shirube has no measured gross alpha at zero fee, so a purely turnover-reducing mechanism can at best move the result toward the static mix and cannot by itself make the strategy profitable; promotion is still decided solely by shirube's own Sharpe/drawdown/trade-count rule on the holdout.
